newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says over 100 firms for African trade fair.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says over 100 firms for African trade fair.

text.p: Nigeria, hosts of the seventh Organisation of African Unity (OAU) trade fair, said on Monday that more than 100 multinational firms had registered and confirmed their participation in the event.

Commerce Minister Rear-Admiral Jubrila Ayinla told reporters at a briefing in Lagos that some of the exhibitors were already at the fair venue in the northern city of Kaduna to begin cosntruction work on their pavilions.
"Also at the last count, a total of 20 OAU member states have booked their stands. I am confident the trade fair will be a huge success," Ayinla said.
The trade fair is due March 29 to April 6 and is expected to feature tourism, agriculture, construction and other sectors.
It was originally scheduled for last year in Lagos but was postponed because of inadequate facilities and moved to Kaduna.

Ayinla said the fair would provide a forum for exchange and dissemination of information on intra-African trade, adding that this has not had the desired impact on the continent's economic development.
"Africa is presently faced with the serious challenges of marginalisation. Thus there is urgent need for African countries to diversify their present trade paterns and look inwards."
The All-Africa trade fair, held every four years, was first hosted by Zaire (formerly Congo) in 1967. The last was held in 1992 in Zimbabwe.
Nigeria has spent more than one billion naira ($12.5 million) to spruce up the venue, the minister said.
